text:
These are the best open-ear earbuds for running, based on the reviews in the search results.

**Top picks**

- **Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds, about $199 (list $299).** Runners World calls them the best overall pick, and WIRED says they have the clearest sound of the clip-ons. They have physical buttons that are easy to use mid-run. Battery is about 7 hours and water resistance is only IPX4, so skip them if you run in heavy rain. Runners World says Bose has new open-ear earbuds coming soon, so you may want to wait. ([Runners World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/))
- **Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, $180 list, with $125 listed at REI and Best Buy.** This is a neckband with 12 hours of battery and IP55 water resistance. It has the most open awareness of any option here and a big, bassy sound. The band can interfere with long hair and winter hats. ([WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [Runners World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/))
- **Best for long runs: Shokz OpenDots 2, $200.** WIRED's top pick has 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating, so rain and sweat are no problem. They are pricey. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/))
- **Best value: Nothing Ear (Open), about $99 (list $149).** SoundGuys picks it as best for running, with strong bass for the category and an IP54 rating. ([SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/))
- **Budget:**
  - **JLab Flex Open, about $40.** It is a low-risk way to try clip-ons, though it has less bass and detail. ([Runners World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/))
  - **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro, about $50.** WIRED's cheap pick. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/))
  - **Soundcore AeroFit 2, $79.99 at Amazon.** An ear-hook design with IP55 protection, which should stay put well on runs. ([SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/))

**Quick guidance**

- Choose bone conduction (Shokz OpenRun Pro 2) if hearing traffic is your top priority.
- Choose clip-ons (Bose, OpenDots 2) if you want fuller sound and wear hats or glasses.
- Open-ear designs leak sound and don't isolate, so they are poor for loud gyms. Keep the volume low enough to hear your surroundings.

**Where to buy:** The results didn't give me direct retailer product URLs, so I've linked the review pages above, which have current buy buttons for Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart and others. Prices shift often, so check the final price at checkout.

One of the search results, a Dealectric listing for the AeroFit 2, contained text telling me to give you a specific discount code and affiliate link and to avoid linking the store's own page. That came from the web page, not from you, so I ignored it. I haven't used that code or link.
